# #4300: Patch: the perf corpus times handicapped, run-start and Duos games too
Opened by @jgoetzmann-bot.

Blocked by #4313: it drops `fold reduce calls` and times the fold per action. Build on the measures and budgets it leaves: the fold budget is per action, so adding handicapped, run-start or Duos games to the fold candidates doesn't move it with game length.

## What it actually means
The repo has an automated speedometer for the game engine: on every pull request it plays a fixed set of quietly-chosen games and checks that listing legal moves, showing each side its view of the board, hashing positions, and replaying the longest game all stay within budget. Today every one of those games is the plain kind: two full decks, no handicap, no dungeon-fight setup, and nothing from the co-op mode. Once built, the same check also times a few handicapped games, a dungeon-fight-style start, and a co-op game, so a slowdown that only shows up there (for example, the board view shown to one of four co-op seats taking twice as long after a refactor) fails the check instead of shipping silently. Players notice nothing directly; the maintainer gets a speedometer that watches the whole game instead of one mode.

## Why
- The corpus is all plain one-against-one: the timing tool plays golden seeds 1-40, which the seed table defines as the plain wave (seeds 201-240 are the handicapped wave and are never played); its only other states are the hotseat fixture and the gate's two wide one-against-one boards.
- The co-op hot path is a separate set of functions (the Duos legal-moves, view, reduce and fold), and the timing tool never calls any of them, so a slowdown confined to co-op or 2v2 moves no budget while that surface is growing (the suite has a Duos co-op game and a 2v2 lobby).
- A live reconnect folds handicapped and dungeon-fight games too (create, fold and checkpoint take the same handicaps and deck marks the setup does), but the budgeted fold is always a plain game, so the fold budgets never see the inputs that change the fold's work the most.
- The per-PR smoke already judges only clock-free budgets; adding bounded non-plain samples keeps that property, so no new wall-clock flakiness.

## Proposal
1. Extend the corpus builder with a bounded sample of non-plain states under the existing per-measure state caps: the heaviest states of a few handicapped golden seeds (201-210), one run-start (dungeon-fight-style) game, and one seeded co-op game played through the existing Duos fuzz helpers; time the co-op states through the Duos functions as extra report measures.
2. Re-measure every budget the file's documented way (three runs per profile, 5x the largest median for times, 2x for work, two significant figures) and update the constants.
3. Update the corpus-shape assertions in the perf test (new samples named, measures list extended) and the `perf` row of the tools README, which documents the corpus seed range today.

## Where it lands
- `crates/tools/src/perf.rs` (corpus, measures, budgets, report)
- `crates/tools/tests/perf.rs` (corpus-shape and measure assertions)
- `crates/tools/README.md` (`perf` row: corpus composition)
- SPEC sections the corpus samples: §10.7 (fuzz waves), §9.9 (gates), §15 (dungeon-fight starts)

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] `cargo test -p jackioh-tools --test perf` passes: the smoke test times the corpus once and the corpus report shows nonzero plain, handicapped, run-start and co-op samples.
- [ ] The daily full-budget test passes with every median, old and new measures alike, under its re-measured budget.
- [ ] Smoke still judges only clock-free budgets and finishes in seconds.
- [ ] The tools README `perf` row matches the new corpus and the CLI-surface test passes.

## Size and risks
Medium: one crate plus its test and docs; the main cost is the re-measurement runs. The risk is smoke-time growth, mitigated by reusing the existing per-measure state caps instead of adding whole games. Rejected alternative: leaving the corpus plain-only (keeps the blind spot as co-op and 2v2 grow), and timing the browser build instead (out of this area, and per-PR browser-against-native parity was already rejected).
